reasoning_summary: The test case fails because the verification logic incorrectly interprets a nested mock call within a verification statement as an actual invocation to be verified. When 'verify(mockTwo).simpleMethod(mock.otherMethod())' is executed, the framework records the call to 'mock.otherMethod()' as part of the verification process. Consequently, when 'verify(mockTwo, never()).simpleMethod(mock.otherMethod())' is called, the framework incorrectly identifies the previous call to 'mock.otherMethod()' as a matching invocation, failing to throw the expected 'NeverWantedButInvoked' exception. This indicates that the framework's internal state tracking for verification is not properly isolating nested mock interactions from the primary verification target.
